subject: Competitive parity & transition playbook - next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Levine <ari@brightlayer.io>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Great demo — draft match term sheet and migration options

Hi Ari — thanks again for the demo yesterday; the team was engaged and we appreciated the detailed perf numbers. Per our ask, I attached a short term sheet that outlines a competitive match + migration assistance option so you have something concrete for procurement to evaluate. High-level: a 20% recurring discount off list for a 12‑month committed tier + a migration credit to cover the first 3 months at current run rate, plus dedicated SRE support for the go‑live window.

Two quick asks from our side: can you confirm who on procurement will own contract redlines, and what your preferred start date for a 12‑month commit would be (we typically see 30–60 day negotiation windows)? If helpful I can loop in Jonas for the SLA / technical handoff.

Attachments: Redwood_Competitive_Match_Term_Sheet.pdf (stub)

Cc: Procurement <procure@brightlayer.io>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Great demo — draft match term sheet and migration options

Vanessa — thanks, appreciate the quick follow. I've looped in procurement (see cc). A couple points up front: our incumbent (CloudArc) has offered us a counter at ~25% below Redwood list for a 12‑month commit and is promising a 2‑week migration window with no billable SRE time. We like Redwood's runtime characteristics but procurement will want to see either price parity or an obvious migration benefit to justify the switch.

Can you clearly state whether Redwood can match the incumbent economics or whether you would need to trade on credits/one‑time assistance? Also: we need clarity on data residency (we require US-only hosting) and evidence of SOC 2. I'm attaching the incumbent quote for reference.

Attachments: CloudArc_quote.pdf

—
Ari Levine
Head of Platform
BrightLayer
ari@brightlayer.io
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightLayer incumbent quote — options

Looping you both with my read: matching a 25% recurring discount off list is tough without a carveout on T&Cs — but we can structure a competitive package that is materially equivalent on first‑year spend. Options to consider (mix & match):

- 20% recurring discount + migration credit equal to the first 3 months of their current spend (applied as invoice credit)
- 15% recurring + 3 months of free dedicated SRE support (on our payroll) + 90‑day SLA uplift (financial credit if latency/availability breach)
- 0% recurring discount but larger committed prepay with tiered rebates and 6‑week migration support (reduces our exposure by locking in revenue)

Operational asks: need to confirm whether BrightLayer requires on‑prem or US‑region only. If it's US‑region we can cover it with our dedicated hosted pools. I'm attaching a deployment checklist to map effort. Also recommend offering a named reference (OrchidHealth) + a pilot per their timeline to reduce procurement risk.

Attachments: deployment-checklist.xlsx

—
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Levine <ari@brightlayer.io>, Procurement <procure@brightlayer.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Great demo — draft match term sheet and migration options

Ari / Procurement — thanks for the transparency, that incumbent quote helps. We can't sustainably match a blanket 25% off list without commitments, but here's a concrete counterproposal designed to be economically equivalent in year‑one while mitigating our risk: 

Counterproposal (example for a 12‑month commit at your current run rate):
- 20% recurring discount to list (applied to committed tier)
- One‑time migration credit equal to 3 months of your current bill (applied as invoice credit)
- Dedicated SRE support included for up to 6 weeks during transition (no separate bill)
- Enhanced SLA for the first 90 days post‑go‑live; financial remedy of up to 5% of monthly invoice for defined breaches
- Fast‑track onboarding: we can guarantee a 45‑day technical handoff window if we sign LOI within 7 business days

I attached an updated term sheet that reflects the above and a short drive link with the migration playbook. If procurement prefers a different mix (larger prepay in exchange for deeper recurring), we can reprice. Can procurement confirm: (1) expected start date for the 12‑month contract, (2) whether US‑only hosting is required, and (3) any internal minimums on financial concessions?

Attachments: Redwood_Competitive_Match_Term_Sheet.pdf
Drive: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/0B7-match-playbook

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Karthik — thanks. Procurement will need the following to proceed to legal review:
1) Final redline‑ready contract (we prefer counter‑redline in DocuSign)
2) Evidence of SOC 2 Type II (or a certificate) and confirmation of US‑region hosting only
3) A customer reference that completed a similar migration in the last 6 months
4) Firm price for a 12‑month committed tier (line item: list price, applied discount, net price)

Attaching our procurement checklist for the record. If you can get the contract and SOC 2 by EOD Friday, we can accelerate legal review and a DocuSign turnaround within 7–10 business days.

Attachments: BrightLayer_procurement_requirements.pdf

Procurement / Ari — acknowledgements and next steps below: 

1) Contract: attaching a redline‑ready SOW + commercial annex (we'll send via DocuSign link). Link: https://app.docusign.com/ClickHere/REDWOOD-BL-1059
2) SOC 2: attaching our public SOC 2 certificate (SOC2_cert_public_v3.pdf). We host BrightLayer in US regions only as part of the dedicated pool option — we'll include the region clause in the annex.
3) Reference: OrchidHealth (Marina Chen, marina@orchidhealth.com) completed an identical migration in March 2026; I've asked Marina to expect a call if you want a technical reference.
4) Firm price (example line): list price $0.0009/token -> 20% discount -> net $0.00072/token for committed tier; migration credit equal to 3 months at current burn will be applied as invoice credit within first 60 days; precise numbers will be filled in the annex once we confirm committed tiers.

I'll queue the DocuSign packet and aim to have the SOC2/contract in procurement's hands by EOD today. If procurement confirms acceptable, can we aim for a 2026‑08‑02 start date? That gives ops 4 weeks after signature for any preflight checks.
